key_insight: A convolutional autoencoder transfer-learning pipeline can learn damage features from large synthetic guided-wave data and adapt to sparse experiments for accurate localization and sizing.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path for structural health monitoring systems where experimental labeling is scarce but reliable damage diagnosis is needed on real plate structures.
method: Generate large pretraining data with a fast 1D time-domain spectral element model.
Pretrain a CAE to learn compact guided-wave features, then transfer to a feed-forward network for diagnosis.
Fine-tune with a small labeled experimental dataset to bridge simulation-to-hardware domain gaps.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong test performance, with R² above 0.93 for damage localization and above 0.99 for damage sizing, including unseen damage cases.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the synthetic simulation domain matches real experimental wave propagation and sensor conditions.
paper_title: A Multi-Fidelity Convolutional Autoencoder-Transfer Learning Framework for Guided-Wave-Based Damage Diagnosis Using Large Simulated and Limited Experimental Datasets
